open_decisions.question: FILEHNDL is a confirmed template (src/templates/program/file-handling.cbl) showing open/process/close and file-status checking for one VSAM and two sequential files; its example paragraphs 2100-READ-VSAM, 2200-WRITE-VSAM and 2300-READ-SEQUENTIAL are never performed (GAP-095). It has no business rules in scope. Is it retired, replaced by a framework file-I/O service, or kept as a developer template?

FILEHNDL is classified template (confirmed): classified as template (confirmed); a human must decide whether it is in modernisation scope. Keep it in the modernisation scope (resolved_no_change) or exclude it (excluded_from_scope)?

Ten elementary level-01 FD/WS items have no permanent Field ID (PORTTRAN WS-EOF-FLAG, TSTGEN00 SEED-RECORD, TSTVAL00 EXPECTED-RECORD/ACTUAL-RECORD/REPORT-RECORD, UTLMNT00 ARCHIVE-RECORD/REPORT-RECORD, UTLVAL00 ERROR-RECORD, FILEHNDL INPUT-RECORD/OUTPUT-RECORD). Should the reverse data agent register Field IDs for record-level elementary items so their Java types can be fixed?

Which character encoding do the DISPLAY files of this batch use (assumed EBCDIC code page 037), and must Java preserve EBCDIC collation for indexed keys such as PORT-KEY, VSAM-RECORD-KEY, POS-KEY and TRAN-KEY?

If FILEHNDL is kept: GAP-024 - on a bad file status the error paragraphs PERFORM 3000-TERMINATE while it or the status check is still active (3000-TERMINATE -> 9000-CHECK-FILE-STATUS -> 9100-VSAM-ERROR -> 3000-TERMINATE, and a second cycle through 9200-SEQ-ERROR); the recursive PERFORM is undefined in standard COBOL. GAP-023 - 2110-PROCESS-VSAM-RECORD (line 122) and 2310-PROCESS-INPUT-RECORD (line 144) do not exist. What termination behaviour is intended on file errors (the source follows with GOBACK and return code 8)?
